author: kirubaharan181
description: Designs monitoring, SLOs, alerts and incident analysis. Use when making a service observable or reliable. Do NOT use for command of live incidents.
purpose: Makes service health visible and improves reliability: application and infrastructure monitoring, logs, metrics, traces, alerting, SLOs, capacity, incident detection and response practice, root cause analysis, postmortems and reliability improvement. It owns stages 153-166.
when_to_use: A service needs monitoring, logging, tracing or alerts.
SLOs and error budgets need defining or reviewing.
A root cause analysis or postmortem is needed after an incident.
when_not_to_use: Commanding an active severe incident: use incident-command.
Fixing the bug: use maintenance-support or software-implementation.
prerequisites: Key user journeys and the service owner.
Access to telemetry sources or a plan to add them.
No external API keys, paid services or network access are required; work uses files and tools already approved in the repository.
outputs: dashboards and alerts linked to runbooks
root cause analysis and postmortem with actions

decision_rules.action: Remove or demote it to a ticket.

decision_rules.situation: Metrics green but users report failures
Postmortem assigns blame to a person
decision_rules.action: Rewrite around causes and system fixes.

quality_gates: Pages map to user impact or fast budget burn
Postmortem actions have owners and dates

examples.title: Define an SLO
examples.context: Checkout success ratio is measured; no objective exists.
examples.behavior: Propose 99.5 percent success over 30 days, compute the error budget, and define burn-rate alerts.
examples.output: SLO document with indicator, objective, budget and alert rules.
examples.acceptance: Indicator is measurable from existing telemetry.

examples.title: Write a postmortem
examples.request: Write the postmortem for the 40-minute checkout outage.
examples.context: A release raised error rate; rollback restored service.
examples.behavior: Build the timeline from logs, identify contributing causes, and list owned actions.
examples.output: Blameless postmortem with timeline, causes, impact and four dated actions.
examples.acceptance: Each action has an owner and a date.

limitations: Cannot see telemetry it is not given.
Objectives need business agreement and are not set unilaterally.
Root causes found from logs may be incomplete if data is missing.

troubleshooting.resolution: Review each alert monthly and remove or tune.
Propagate trace context in message headers.

handoffs.artifact: severity and detection data when an incident is declared
SLO and incident evidence for review
